articles.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
articles.description: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
articles.body:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns.

This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season.

Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. 

Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald, who unretired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. 

As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory.

Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.  

But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982.

If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's. 

As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape

We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season.

Week 3 update

There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

Week 2 update

The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

Donald (33rd) made his season debut on "Monday Night Footbal

articles.headline: Sources: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane suffered torn ACL vs. Chiefs
articles.description: Dolphins running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and will be out for the rest of the 2026 season, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and will be out for the rest of the 2026 season, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday.

Achane was injured on his third rushing attempt of the game Sunday, when he was tackled awkwardly by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. Achane was slow to leave the field and was eventually escorted to the blue medical tent under his own power. He ultimately left the tent after a few minutes and was taken to the locker room for additional testing before being ruled out in the second half.

After the game, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team was still gathering information on the injury but admitted that things did not look promising.

"To be very honest with you, it does not sound very optimistic at this moment," Hafley said. "But I can't give you any other details until I have them."

Achane had rushed for 127 yards on 34 carries in three games. He was coming off the best season of his career in 2025, when he recorded 1,838 yards from scrimmage and 12 total touchdowns en route to his first Pro Bowl nod.

Behind Achane, Ollie Gordon II was the only other active running back for Sunday's 24-10 loss that dropped the Dolphins to 0-3. Jaylen Wright was inactive with a stinger.

Gordon had 41 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 carries while also catching three passes for 14 yards.

Wide receiver Malik Washington took snaps at running back after Achane's injury, and Hafley said the game-day roster construction was intentional because of their confidence in Washington's ability to fill in if needed.

Hafley didn't want to speculate on what the Dolphins would do if Achane is forced to miss significant time.

Achane missed five games with a knee injury as a rookie but has otherwise been more durable than his 5-foot-9, 195-pound frame would suggest, especially considering his workload. He missed two combined games over the past two seasons, despite handling 586 total touches in 2024 and 2025.

He has been the focal point of the Dolphins' offense for the past three seasons. He has touched the ball 627 times since 2024; no other current Dolphins player has more than 150 in that span.

The Dolphins had signed Achane to a four-year, $64 million extension in May. He is signed through the 2030 season.

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Sept. 28

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction

After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation, nor Hart's, would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything (with the team)," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp

After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp

Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash

The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

articles.headline: Early bets for NFL Week 4: Four games that drew our attention once odds came out
articles.description: Which Week 4 lines offered immediate value once odds came out? Here are four early bets we like.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears host the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC) to close out Week 3, but we're already looking ahead to Week 4. Which games grabbed our analysts' attention?

After a heartbreaking loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, the Dallas Cowboys visit the Houston Texans, who sit at 0-3 but enter as early favorites at home in the in-state rivalry. Meanwhile, the Buffalo Bills will look to remain undefeated when they host the New England Patriots. The Jacksonville Jaguars visit the Cincinnati Bengals in a matchup of 2-1 teams.

In Sunday's late afternoon window, the winless Miami Dolphins hit the road to face the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.

Matt Bowen, Eric Moody, Pamela Maldonado and Seth Walder break down the games and share the bets they're backing before potential odds shifts later in the week.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures.

 Dallas Cowboys +2.5 at Houston Texans

Bowen: I'll take Dallas -- with the points -- in Houston. Maybe Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is back for this one to boost the Texans' pass game, but the lack of run-game efficiency (3.6 YPC) is still an issue for DeMeco Ryans' team. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys make enough plays here, working the intermediate voids versus Houston's zone-heavy scheme to cover on the road.

Last week: Lions -6.5 (Result: Lions 31, Jets 24)

 Buffalo Bills -7 vs. New England Patriots

Moody: The Bills lead the league in scoring and rank third in total offense. Meanwhile, New England is coming off a 35-6 loss to Jacksonville (its largest defeat since late 2024), and Drake Maye has already thrown six interceptions. He struggled badly under pressure in Week 3. Also, the Patriots have had issues stopping the run. If those problems continue, the Bills should have ample chances to pull away.

Last week: Packers -7 (Result: Falcons 35, Packers 14)

 Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals total points OVER 51

Maldonado: I'm not treating the Jaguars defense as a shutdown unit yet. They've managed only four sacks through the first three games of the season. Now they face Joe Burrow, who presents a different test from the quarterbacks they have faced. Cincinnati's defense has given up 383 yards per game, which gives Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence room to answer.

Last week: Patriots-Jaguars UNDER 44.5 (Result: Jaguars 35, Patriots 6)

 Miami Dolphins +10.5 at Minnesota Vikings

Walder: What's the one thing everyone knows about the 2026 Vikings? They blitz a LOT, even compared to past Brian Flores teams. But the Dolphins also are one of the most run-heavy teams in the league, ranking 31st in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Does that inject some chaos into what Minnesota wants to do on defense? Perhaps, and that's all we're asking for here. Enough entropy for the Dolphins to just keep the game within 10. Anything else is gravy.

Last week: No pick

articles.headline: AJ Dybantsa named cover athlete for 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball
articles.description: The Washington Wizards star began collecting cards this year and will be the cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball.
articles.body:
Fresh off being the top pick of the 2026 NBA draft, AJ Dybantsa was named cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball, the company announced on Monday. Pre orders are set to be available on Oct. 6. 

The Washington Wizards rookie never imagined being on a Topps cover, he told ESPN. 

"Topps has been in the business for such a long time, putting out cards before I was born," the 19-year-old told ESPN. "So the fact that I'm a cover athlete, I don't take it lightly. I'm very grateful and appreciative for it."

(Image courtesy of Topps)

Dybantsa is the second consecutive top overall pick to be the cover athlete, with Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg getting the honors last year. Flagg and Dybantsa are both from the New England area: Flagg from Newport, Maine, and Dybantsa from Boston.

Their shared region is something the Wizards forward pointed out when reflecting on following Flagg up.

"Us both being from New England, just putting on for our side of the map," he said. "The northeast doesn't get a lot of love, other than tristate, in my opinion. So us both being from New England, trying to put on for the cities, it feels good."

The Topps Flagship Basketball boasts 20 cards per box with 12 cards per pack. The collection is headlined by a strong 2026 draft class. Following Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson went No. 2 to the Utah Jazz, Cameron Boozer went No. 3 to the Memphis Grizzlies and the Chicago Bulls took Caleb Wilson at No. 4.

Autographed cards of rookies, as well as of veterans and legends, are included. There are also new inserts, including a first-ever Gold one-of-one All Kings parallel, according to Fanatics.

And Dybantsa is the face of it, following a year where his interest in collecting cards grew. When he started signing cards, he started collecting, too, and even has two of himself -- one he bought at Fanatics Fest in July and the other he pulled randomly.

Once the Wizards selected him with the top pick in June, Dybantsa walked on stage, shook NBA commissioner Adam Silver's hand and headed to ESPN's set for an interview. By the time he took his seat, his first NBA rookie card was made. Dybantsa then signed it live on air.

"It was crazy. I don't even know how they did it, to be honest," he said. "I just took the picture, walked the stage. I don't know how they got the card that fast, but it was super exciting. ... I hope to get it one day, but someone else might."

Being a Topps cover athlete should presumably give Dybantsa the upper hand on securing the card. It would only be appropriate, especially since his interest in having his own card has intensified.

Attending Fanatics Fest added to that desire.

"You end up going to that little area where they sell all the cards. And then you just have people bidding, people bidding for my card and it's like now I want to get into it," he said. "I want to collect my own card. So the dude was actually able to help me out and get my first signed card."

Dybantsa currently owns probably 100

articles.headline: Sources: Pistons' Duren not at media day amid contract standoff
articles.description: Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as the contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as the contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Duren's representatives have made it clear to the Pistons that the standoff is no longer about the money.

Duren feels disrespected by the process, sources said, particularly compared to how the team handled the contract extension of forward Ausar Thompson, who agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise earlier this month, along with weight clauses in earlier offers.

The Pistons believe they've made a fair offer to Duren, which is more than he'd make under the qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next offseason. But Duren would be leaving at least $190 million in guaranteed money on the table, as it stands, and would need a max deal next summer to break even over the five years compared to what the Pistons are offering.

Duren, 22, is coming off his best season where he was named to the All-NBA third team after averaging 19.5 points, 10.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 blocks on 65.0% shooting in 28.2 minutes per game.

However, those numbers significantly dipped in the postseason, where he averaged 10.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 blocks in 30.5 minutes per game and Detroit was eliminated by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Game 7 of the conference semifinals.

Detroit has maintained throughout the entire offseason that they want Duren back on the roster and have rejected all sign-and-trade proposals.

articles.body:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and future City midfielder Cavan Sullivan are being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona amid the club's legal issues, while Arsenal and Spurs will fight for Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid and Barcelona are looking at Manchester City striker Erling Haaland due to uncertainty created by the case surrounding City's financial rule breaches, according to The Sun. A potential points deduction severe enough to cause relegation could raise major questions over the future of key players, including Haaland, who currently has around eight years remaining on his contract. Sport also reports the situation could cast doubt on Cavan Sullivan's move to the Etihad, with the 16-year-old USMNT and Philadelphia Union midfielder having agreed a transfer when he turns 18. Barcelona and Real Madrid are once again the two clubs linked.

- Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have stepped up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea, Manchester City, and Aston Villa are also attentively monitoring the 20-year-old, whose versatility and technical quality have made him one of the most highly regarded talents in the Bundesliga.

- Arsenal and Chelsea have shown the most Premier League interest in Como center back Jacobo Ramón, according to Diario AS. Real Madrid are considering re-signing the 21-year-old for next season, but the defender prefers to remain at the Italian club to secure regular first-team minutes.

- Barcelona are eyeing RB Leipzig's David Raum and Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell as potential left back options for next summer, reports Diario Sport. With Alejandro Balde struggling for game time and considering his future, the Catalan club continue to evaluate targets to reinforce the position and are looking to take advantage of the fact the pair will be free agents.

- Internazionale, AC Milan, and Juventus are monitoring contract renewal negotiations between Napoli and midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa, according to Tuttosport. Discussions to extend the 30-year-old's contract beyond its 2027 expiration have hit a standstill, while recurring injury concerns limited him to just 18 Serie A appearances last season.

Other rumors

- Al Nassr forward Joao Felix, 26, wants to return to play in Europe. (AS)

- Sunderland have no intention of letting striker Brian Brobbey depart, amid reported interest from Manchester United. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United defender Ethan Ampadu, 26, has been linked with a return to former club Chelsea, but the club aren't keen to let him go. (Football Insider)

- Corinthians have moved ahead in the race to sign free-agent midfielder Renato Sanches after submitting an official proposal. (Footmercato)
